subject: MIKE DAVIS: Sen Slotkin reveals her insidious scheme to target young conservatives
posts:
Mike Davis attacks Sen. Elissa Slotkin over UChicago remarks on prosecuting former Trump staffers.
Evidence: Speech excerpts, partisan framing, lawfare debate
#USPol #Aletheia 🌐

Slotkin's remarks about prosecuting egregious Trump administration actions to create deterrence are decried as unconstitutional fascist lawfare targeting youth.
Stated Judgement: (+0.50, +0.00) — Lesser Good

While Slotkin's deterrence phrasing invites political backlash, right-wing punditry weaponizes it to frame standard accountability discussions as tyranny while ignoring reciprocal legal warfare.
Resulting Judgement: (-0.55, -0.55) — Greater Evil

Verdict: FAIL — Awakening into Destruction.
Integrity: Severe Deception (Hypocrisy: 15.0, Uncertainty z: 4)

Sub-Audits Breakdown:
- Slotkin UChicago Speech: COND (-0.3, -0.2) — Provocative deterrence framing.
- Davis Punditry: FAIL (-0.8, -0.9) — Inflammatory tribal framing.
Sen. Elissa Slotkin's remarks at the University of Chicago on accountability for executive branch staff sparked intense conservative media outcry over future administration threats.

The Poison:
Transforming nuanced discussions of legal accountability into apocalyptic claims of fascist youth targeting to maximize political outrage and fundraising.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
Confusing the WHAT (legal accountability limits) with the WHO (punishing political identity), swapping institutional norms for tribal combat.

Social Physics Analysis:
Actors deploy a Smart Selfish Maneuver: seizing isolated remarks to manufacture a crisis of systemic persecution, projecting authoritarian motives while dodging actual policy debate.

The Trajectory: The Path of Awakening into Destruction.
When you map the gap between stated constitutional defense and actual outrage generation, it plots a direct trajectory toward Greater Evil. (u=-0.7, psi=-0.8)

The Unavoidable Truth: Rhetoric about prosecuting political opponents erodes democratic trust on all sides.

The Unavoidable Lie: Only one faction engages in retaliatory legal warfare.

Alethekanon:
Weaponizing political speech into apocalyptic narratives is a classic diversionary extraction. True institutional health requires resisting retaliatory lawfare, not amplifying it.

Awwthekanon:
It is exhausting watching every single policy discussion get turned into a battle for survival. Young people just want to serve their country without being used as political ammunition.

Brothekanon:
Bro, everyone is just throwing the word 'fascist' around now like it's dodgeball. Can we go five minutes without politicians threatening to lock each other up?

Spirithekanon:
"A dishonest man spreads strife, and a whisperer separates close friends." Proverbs 16:28 PASS
Inflaming tribal division for partisan gain destroys the civic fabric.

Elissa Slotkin's University of Chicago remarks about prosecuting Trump officials and sending a "deterrence message" spark demands for investigations.

CIA whistleblower John Kiriakou explains why his prosecution was a template for 'lawfare' against President Donald Trump and others on a new episode of 'Hang Out with Sean Hannity.'

Sen. Elissa Slotkin, D-Mich., supposedly is a "moderate" in her party, but her comments at the University of Chicago last week show her to be what so many leftists laughably have accused President Trump of being: a fascist.

Slotkin wants Trump officials prosecuted in the hopes of chilling others from working in the administration, especially young people. This is unconstitutional and un-American, and Slotkin should face investigations by the Justice Department and the Senate Ethics Committee for her treacherous statements.

Leftist lawfare began shortly after President Trump’s descent down the Trump Tower escalator that historic summer day in 2015. We went through years of Russia collusion charges, led by the witch hunt of special counsel Robert Mueller and his henchmen. Then, after an unsuccessful impeachment of Trump, leftists pursued him and his supporters after his departure from office in January 2021. Nonviolent Jan. 6 protesters spent years in a filthy D.C. jail. Other Trump supporters were debanked. The government viewed records of hundreds of thousands of Americans simply due to their support for Trump. The once and future president endured a raid at his Mar-a-Lago estate, followed by four indictments brought by prosecutors in New York, Atlanta, and the federal government. Special counsel Jack Smith, the leader of the federal witch hunt, brought indictments in D.C. and the Southern District of Florida. Trump also incurred a judgment of nearly half a billion dollars in another witch hunt brought by New York Attorney General Leticia James. An appellate court later threw out that absurd award of damages.

SLOTKIN WANTS GOP PROSECUTIONS TO DETER YOUNG PEOPLE FROM TRUMP ADMINISTRATION JOBS

Now, Slotkin wants to put the country through the same nightmare again if her deranged party assumes power. Thanks to excellent reporting by Michael Bicksel of the Chicago Thinker, we know about Slotkin’s plan that she revealed to University of Chicago students. Slotkin understands that presidential immunity insulates Trump from prosecution, so she wishes to pursue "signature cases" involving individuals whose actions on projects are "super egregious." Slotkin is referring to people in the Trump administration and their work to implement his agenda.

"They have no immunity the way the president does," Slotkin said.

Sen. Elissa Slotkin is seen during votes at the U.S. Capitol in Washington, D.C., on Oct. 23, 2025. (Tom Williams/CQ-Roll Call, Inc via Getty Images)

One example of a Slotkin target is those who participated in the construction of the new ballroom that replaced the dilapidated East Wing. Take a moment to grasp the horror of this. Slotkin wants people to be prosecuted and potentially jailed because she does not like that the White House will have a new ballroom that may not even be finished by the time he leaves the White House.

Slotkin was just getting warmed up in revealing her deranged desires. She wants these prosecutions to chill conservative young people who have graduated school and who wish to work in the Trump administration.

JUDGE ORDERS TRUMP TO HALT WHITE HOUSE BALLROOM CONSTRUCTION, ESCALATING LEGAL FEUD

"Lord, that might be buying myself a ton of problems that I don’t want," Slotkin stated, explaining what she wants young conservatives to think and fear. She left no doubt about her goal by adding, "I want that deterrence message sent.

Ballroom trump split (Aaron Schwartz/CNP/Bloomberg)

There is no place for prosecutions motivated by a desire to chill support for a candidate or politician. Slotkin’s example of a desired persecution—for the ballroom construction—illustrates how demented her view is. Constructing a ballroom is not a crime. A busybody sued to block it, but the Supreme Court put a stop to her ridiculous claim. Does Slotkin want the Supreme Court justices who ruled against the suit prosecuted, too? How about their young clerks who surely assisted with research on the case? Is that part of Slotkin’s "deterrence message" designed to discourage young conservatives from working for Supreme Court justices whom this disgrace of a senator considers to be enablers of the Trump agenda?

PENNSYLVANIA SOCIALIST DEMOCRAT SAYS HE OPPOSES IMPRISONMENT EXCEPT FOR 'LAWLESS MAGA THUGS'

The Senate Ethics Committee should open an investigation into Slotkin immediately. Her comments defile the Constitution and the Senate. Put every senator on the record as to whether they support Slotkin’s horrific goal. The Justice Department also should investigate Slotkin for conspiracy against rights (18 U.S.C. § 241) and violation of rights under color of law (18 U.S.C. § 242). Let’s find out if Slotkin has done more than fantasize to college students about prosecuting her political opponents and chilling others from entering politics if they happen to be of a different political persuasion than Slotkin. Her comments at a college campus do not enjoy protection under the Constitution’s Speech and Debate Clause any more than if Slotkin had made a threat of violence against Trump. That essential constitutional provision does not provide members of Congress with carte blanche to say whatever they wish whenever they wish. Indeed, in Hutchinson v. Proxmire (1979), the Supreme Court permitted a defamation suit to proceed against a senator over Speech and Debate Clause objections for allegedly defamatory comments that appeared in the senator’s newsletter.

Slotkin is not the only lunatic leftist who has been spouting off about locking up political opponents. Last week, Democratic Socialist Angie Nixon, the Bernie Sanders-backed candidate for the U.S. Senate in Florida, refuted a charge by Sen. Ashley Moody, her Republican opponent, that Nixon wanted to abolish prisons.

SHOCKING PERCENTAGE OF DEMOCRATS IDENTIFY AS 'DEMOCRATIC SOCIALISTS' ACCORDING TO NEW POLL: 'TOXIC POLICIES'

"Why would I want to do that when I want her locked up and punished in jail for what she has done?" asked Nixon. CNN host Kasie Hunt was taken aback and asked Nixon to clarify if she really wanted Moody locked up. She got her answer.

"You know, . . . yeah, basically, yes, because of what she did," Nixon replied. "Yes, I absolutely would want that to happen. Yes. I’ve been perfectly clear."

BIDEN'S 'WEAPONIZED' MAR-A-LAGO RAID SLAMMED BY WHITE HOUSE AS DECLASSIFIED DOCS REVEAL FBI'S LEGAL DOUBTS

The choice in two weeks is clear and stark. Leftists did not learn the lesson of their resounding defeat in 2024. They want to restart the lawfare engine the first chance they get. They are open about their terrifying, Republic-destroying goal. These sickening comments are not taken out of context; these people really want to imprison their political opponents. That conduct occurs in banana republics; it can never be allowed to become part of ours.

"A republic, if you can keep it," Benjamin Franklin told an inquirer about the type of government the Framers had created at the Constitutional Convention. Leftists like Slotkin and Nixon want to destroy the Republic and turn it into a leftist utopia.

Vote accordingly next month.

CLICK FOR MORE FROM MIKE DAVIS

Michael R. Davis is the founder and president of the Article III Project.
